title: Every screenshot is on the clipboard, every time, and pastes everywhere
goal: Since about 2026-11-01 a screenshot taken with Photonz is not reliably on the clipboard: sometimes the paste that follows gets nothing or the old clipboard. Copying a capture to the clipboard is the heart of the app; it must work every single time, into every kind of app, however fast the paste follows.
notes: User, 2026-11-03 (intake): 'lately when i take a screenshot, it isn't reliably copying it to clipboard. it's rather annoying. i think something regressed. make sure that screenshots are copied to clipboard reliably'. Timing matches e0648dd9 (shipped in v0.22.0). Code: Sources/Photonz/Capture/CaptureStore.swift (add: handOffNewScreenshot before writePNG; the later copy skipped when handedOff.changeCount still matches), Sources/Photonz/ClipboardHandOff.swift (promised types made in the background, then handed to the system clipboard type by type), Sources/PhotonzRender/ClipboardPicture.swift. Not reproduced yet by the intake window.
acceptance: Reproduce first, and say how often it fails and how. Take screenshots the ways the person does (each capture shortcut and mode: region, window, full screen, the menu bar icon) and paste into a native app (Preview, Pages or Notes), a browser text field (Chrome or Safari), an Electron chat app (Slack or Teams), Finder, Mail and Claude, at once and after 1 s and 10 s. At least 20 captures per kind of target. Record each failure: what the clipboard held (types and sizes, read with NSPasteboard from a second process) and what the target pasted.

Find the cause before fixing. Prime suspect: e0648dd9 (2026-11-01, 'Copy is on the clipboard the instant you press it'), which changed the capture path to put a new screenshot on the clipboard BEFORE its file is written (CaptureStore.add, handOffNewScreenshot) and to PROMISE its PNG and TIFF through ClipboardHandOff, handing the data over later. Check at least: (1) the file URL goes up before the file exists, so targets that read the file URL first (Finder, Mail, Claude, Slack, Teams) can paste a missing or half written file; (2) setting data on an item already on the pasteboard after a promise, which AppKit may ignore, leaving a promised type with no provider (pasteboardFinishedWithDataProvider) and nothing behind it; (3) a paste that asks a promised type while Photonz's main thread is busy finishing the capture times out empty; (4) the capture's own later copy being skipped by the changeCount check when it should not be. Run git bisect against v0.21.0 if the cause is not plain.

Fix it so a screenshot pastes correctly in every target above, 20 of 20 for each, immediately and later, including while Photonz is busy. Never offer a file URL for a file that does not exist yet: write the file first, or leave the URL off until it exists and add it then.
Keep what e0648dd9 fixed: an editor Copy still updates the clipboard within one frame, and a paste that comes first still gets the new picture (its Scripts/clipboard-timing measures must still pass).
A walk or script that takes captures and pastes into a second process repeatedly, kept in the repo, so this cannot regress silently again; numbers before and after in the audit under queue/audits/.
Anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar (queue/bin/follow-up-bar.md), and written into this task's log if it does not.
